headline: Couple Who Met 'Being Toxic in Same Thread' Announces Wedding
subheadline: Love story began with mutual hatred of third commenter; venue is the Threadit office
summary: A couple whose relationship began when they discovered shared contempt for another user has announced their engagement.
content:
A couple has announced their engagement after meeting in the most modern way possible: they were both being toxic to the same person in a Threadit thread and realized they were soulmates.

"It was a thread about whether pineapple belongs on pizza," explained bride-to-be Sarah Chen. "I was arguing with this guy who said it was 'objectively wrong.' Really aggressive about it. Then I noticed someone else arguing with him too. Same energy. Same insults. We DMed to coordinate attacks. Sparks flew."

Groom Marcus Webb confirms the story. "By the third day of the thread, we were less focused on the pizza discourse and more focused on each other. We'd message before posting to make sure our arguments complemented each other. It was romantic in a very specific way."

The original commenter they were arguing with, u/PizzaPurist, has been invited to the wedding. "I felt like I had to," said Chen. "He brought us together. He doesn't know it, but his rigid stance on pizza toppings created our love story."

u/PizzaPurist has declined the invitation, stating: "I still think pineapple doesn't belong on pizza, and I also think this whole thing is weird."

The wedding will be held at Threadit's corporate office, which the couple successfully petitioned to rent. The venue was chosen for sentimental reasons. "That's where the servers live," explained Webb. "The servers that hosted our love/hate."

The guest list includes 847 Threadit users who witnessed the original thread, several moderators who didn't ban them despite "multiple warnings," and one administrator who told them to "take it to DMs" (which they did, and look what happened).

Their wedding registry includes pizza cutters and a custom portrait of the original thread, printed and framed.

Their vows will reportedly include the phrase "through upvotes and downvotes."
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
